name: Slack Approval Gate — Human In The Loop

parameters.content:
## Slack Approval Gate

Puts a person in front of anything irreversible. The workflow pauses on the Slack node until someone clicks a button, then continues down the approved or declined branch.

**Why this is worth the five minutes:** it converts your worst-case outcome from "the automation emailed 400 customers" into "someone clicked Decline." Add it in front of every send, charge, delete, or post.

Especially worth it in front of anything an AI agent decided to do.

parameters.content:
### Two settings that matter

**Approval type is `double`** — the Slack message shows both Approve and Decline. Approve-only cannot distinguish "declined" from "nobody looked yet", and that ambiguity is the whole reason you added a gate.

**Waiting executions survive restarts** only if your instance persists them — one more reason to run Postgres rather than SQLite for anything real.

If approvals routinely go unanswered, add a timeout branch. An execution waiting forever is its own kind of silent failure.
